title: Carpet-Bombing DDoS: The Attack Pattern Your Per-IP Defenses Won’t Catch
summary: On Apr 28, 2026, a regional ISP in South Asia was hit by carpet-bombing attacks across 25 IPs in 40 minutes. Read how the evasion unfolded.
body_text: DDoS Carpet-bombing Attack Unfolds in Real Time. Here’s What It Looked Like. 25 Ips, one subnet, 40 minutes, and your per-IP rate limiter didn’t see a thing A Quiet Morning in South Asia At 07:35 UTC on April 28, 2026, a regional ISP in South Asia started taking fire. Not the kind of fire that trips alarms. No single IP experienced a traffic spike dramatic enough to cross a typical per-IP detection threshold. But something far more deliberate was underway. Over the next 40 minutes, we watched through A10 Defend Threat Control as attackers systematically walked through more than 25 distinct IP addresses within a single /24 subnet, hitting each one with high-complexity NTP amplification. A new target every 30 to 90 seconds. Each attack lasted anywhere from 21 seconds to nearly 8 minutes. Then the attacker moved on to the next address. This is carpet-bombing and it is one of the most effective DDoS evasion techniques in use today. What Carpet-bombing Looks Like in the Data Here is a condensed view of the attack timeline, pulled directly from the A10 Defend Threat Control victim data. Every row is a separate attack event. Every IP belongs to the same /24 owned by the same regional broadband provider. Time (UTC) Victim IP (Masked) Duration Vector 07:35:17 160.250.82.x (.45) 21 sec NTP – High 07:35:41 160.250.82.x (.242) 404 sec NTP – High 07:36:16 160.250.82.x (.115) 57 sec NTP – High 07:37:14 160.250.82.x (.56) 80 sec NTP – High 07:38:36 160.250.82.x (.207) 54 sec NTP – High 07:39:32 160.250.82.x (.43) 63 sec NTP – High 07:40:40 160.250.82.x (.232) 37 sec NTP – High 07:42:27 160.250.82.x (.176) 49 sec NTP – High 07:43:20 160.250.82.x (.141) 354 sec NTP – High 07:44:26 160.250.82.x (.70) 56 sec NTP – High 07:45:25 160.250.82.x (.215) 77 sec NTP – High 07:46:44 160.250.82.x (.254) 29 sec NTP – High 07:47:15 160.250.82.x (.229) 67 sec NTP – High 07:49:16 160.250.82.x (.85) 88 sec NTP – High 07:50:51 160.250.82.x (.117) 37 sec NTP – High … … (25+ IPs total) … … 08:01:14 160.250.82.x (.131) 479 sec NTP – High Figure: Condensed timeline of the carpet-bombing campaign. Full dataset available in A10 Defend Threat Control. Notice the pattern. No single IP accumulates enough traffic to dominate a dashboard. The attacker distributes the pain across the entire subnet, ensuring that the aggregate bandwidth hitting the victim’s upstream link is enormous, even though each individual target looks only moderately busy. Why This Matters More Than You Think Carpet-bombing exploits a fundamental assumption baked into most DDoS detection systems: that attacks concentrate on a single destination. Traditional mitigation triggers on per-IP volumetric thresholds. When traffic to a single IP spikes, you scrub it. Simple. But what happens when no single IP crosses the threshold? When the attacker instead sends 40 Gbps spread across 25 IPs, each absorbing just 1.6 Gbps. Individually, those flows might sit below your alerting baseline. Collectively, they saturate the upstream link and take the entire subnet offline. This is not theoretical. In this campaign, the targeted ISP’s entire /24 was under sustained NTP amplification for 40 continuous minutes. The longest single-IP attack lasted nearly 8 minutes (479 seconds), but the campaign lasted far longer because the attacker simply rotated targets. The Clues Were There—If You Knew Where to Look What made this campaign visible in A10 Defend Threat Control was not any single attack event, but the correlation across events. The platform captures victim data across all observed attacks globally, which means patterns that span multiple IPs, subnets, and time windows become visible in a way they never would from a single vantage point. When we queried the data for this /24, the carpet-bombing pattern jumped out immediately: same ASN, same attack vector, same complexity rating, tightly clustered timestamps, and sequential IP targeting. An analyst looking at any individual event would see a routine 60-second NTP hit. An analyst looking at the subnet-level pattern would see an orchestrated campaign. That difference—between seeing one event and seeing the campaign—is the difference between reacting and anticipating. “An analyst looking at one event sees a routine NTP hit. An analyst looking at the subnet sees an orchestrated campaign. That gap is where carpet-bombing lives.” What Should Defenders Do? Think in subnets, not just IPs. If your detection logic only evaluates per-destination thresholds, carpet-bombing will fly under the radar. Aggregate traffic analysis at the /24 or prefix level is essential. Correlate across time windows. A 60-second NTP attack is unremarkable. Twenty-five of them against the same subnet in 40 minutes is a campaign. Your tooling needs to surface that pattern automatically. Use external threat intelligence. The victim ISP in this case may not have had visibility into the broader pattern. They only see their own ingress. A platform like A10 Defend Threat Control provides the global vantage point that turns isolated alerts into actionable intelligence. Assume NTP amplification isn’t going away. Every attack in this campaign used NTP reflection at high complexity. Open NTP servers continue to provide massive amplification, and attackers know it. See it for Yourself This carpet-bombing campaign is just one pattern we surfaced from over one million DDoS attacks observed by A10 Defend Threat Control in April 2026 alone. The platform lets you filter by attack type, victim country, ASN, industry, duration, and more, turning raw data into the kind of intelligence that keeps you ahead of the next campaign. Explore the live data on the A10 Defend Threat Control dashboard or sign up for a 90-day free trial to see what attackers are doing right now. Our Corporate Banking division has recently hired Joe Cook, and Matt Garrity and Shane Weissman have joined Venture Lending. Joe Cook joined as Senior Vice President to strengthen Avidbank's Bay Area presence serving small- to mid-sized businesses. He brings more than 20 years of commercial banking experience in the San Francisco Bay area, with a focus on C&I and owner-occupied real estate. The addition of both Matt Garrity and Shane Weissman, who are based in New York City, will help expand Avidbank's Venture Lending presence on the east coast. Mr. Garrity joins as Senior Vice President and has over 20 years of banking experience. Mr. Weissman is joining as Vice President and has over 10 years' experience in venture banking. "We've always taken a deliberate approach to growth and therefore need to be opportunistic when it comes to talent," said Mark D. Mordell, Chairman and CEO of Avidbank. "The caliber of Joe, Matt and Shane certainly will be a great complement to our outstanding team." About Avidbank Avidbank Holdings, Inc. body_text: VSE Corporation Completes Acquisition of Precision Aviation Group May 05, 2026 7:30am EDT Download as PDF Acquisition increases VSE revenue by ~50% on a pro forma 2025 basis; expected to be immediately accretive to VSE’s Adjusted EBITDA margins MIRAMAR, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- VSE Corporation (NASDAQ: VSEC), a leading provider of aviation aftermarket distribution and repair services, today announced it has completed the acquisition of Precision Aviation Group, Inc. (“PAG”), a portfolio company of GenNx360 Capital Partners (“GenNx”), for approximately $2.025 billion in cash and equity. The combination creates a scaled, independent aviation aftermarket platform with 61 locations across 8 countries, including 48 repair facilities and 11 distribution centers. The expanded platform enhances VSE’s global reach, technical capabilities, and integrated offering across maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services and distribution, serving a diverse customer base across commercial, business and general aviation, rotorcraft, original equipment manufacturer, and defense markets. CEO Commentary “Today marks a significant milestone in executing our strategy to build a focused, high-quality aviation aftermarket platform,” said John Cuomo, President and Chief Executive Officer of VSE. “The addition of PAG meaningfully expands our global footprint, strengthens our repair capabilities, and enhances our ability to deliver integrated, end-to-end solutions to our customers. “With the transaction closed, our focus shifts to integration and synergy realization through cross-selling, repair insourcing, and procurement efficiencies. PAG’s margin profile is immediately accretive and supports a clear path to exceeding 20% consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margins over time.” “Importantly, we are excited to welcome the talented PAG team to the VSE family and look forward to their contributions as we move forward together,” Cuomo concluded. Transaction Details The $2.025 billion purchase price includes $1.75 billion in cash and approximately $275 million in equity issued to GenNx that is exchangeable for VSE common stock, and up to an additional $125 million in contingent earnout payment based on 2026 performance, which is payable in cash, VSE common stock, or a combination thereof, at VSE’s discretion. The transaction was funded using the net proceeds from VSE’s February 2026 equity and tangible equity unit offerings and $900 million under a new Term Loan B maturing in 2033. VSE will provide additional detail on the combined company’s outlook, capital structure, and integration priorities with its first-quarter earnings release on May 5, 2026. VSE Advisors Perella Weinberg Partners served as exclusive financial and debt capital markets advisor to VSE. Jones Day served as legal counsel to VSE. RBC Capital Markets served as lead-left arranger on VSE’s Term Loan B. Citizens Bank, N.A. served as administrative agent for the syndicate banks supporting the revolving credit facility. ABOUT VSE CORPORATION VSE is a leading provider of aviation distribution and repair services for the commercial and B&GA aftermarkets. Headquartered in Miramar, Florida, VSE is focused on significantly enhancing the productivity and longevity of its customers' high-value, business-critical assets. VSE’s aftermarket parts distribution and maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services support engine component and engine and airframe accessory part distribution and repair services for commercial and B&GA operators. For more detailed information, please visit VSE's website at www.vsecorp.com . ABOUT PRECISION AVIATION GROUP Precision Aviation Group (“PAG”) is a leading global provider of aviation aftermarket MRO, distribution, and supply chain services supporting B&GA, rotorcraft, and defense markets. PAG serves a broad global customer base and delivers technical expertise across engines, components, avionics, and proprietary repair solutions. NON-GAAP MEASURES In addition to the financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), this release also contains non-GAAP financial measures. These measures provide useful information to investors. VSE considers VSE’s Adjusted EBITDA margin as non-GAAP financial measure and an important indicator of performance and useful metric for management and investors to evaluate VSE’s business' ongoing operating performance on a consistent basis across reporting periods. This non-GAAP financial measure, however, should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for performance measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. VSE Adjusted EBITDA margin represents estimated operating income before depreciation and amortization expenses as a percentage of revenue. Management believes Adjusted EBITDA margin provides useful information about the Company's operating performance as it isolates non-cash depreciation and amortization charges as well as interest expense and income taxes, which are non-operating items. Additionally, VSE Adjusted EBITDA margin is presented as a forward-looking non-GAAP financial measure based solely on information available to VSE as of the date of this press release and may differ materially from VSE’s actual operating results as a result of developments that occur after the date of this press release. The determination of the amounts that are excluded from this non-GAAP financial measure is a matter of management judgment and depends upon, among other factors, the nature of the underlying expense, income amounts or anticipated synergies recognized in a given period. VSE is unable to present a quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking VSE Adjusted EBITDA to net income because certain information regarding the Company’s provision for income taxes is not available, and management cannot reliably predict all of the necessary components of net income at this time without unreasonable effort or expense. title: Scorpio Tankers Inc. Announces Proposed Reopening of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 and Concurrent Stock Repurchase
summary: MONACO, May 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Scorpio Tankers Inc. (NYSE: STNG) (the “Company”) announced today its intention to offer $150.0 million aggregate principal amount of additional 1.75% convertible senior [...]
body_text: Back to all Scorpio Tankers Inc. Announces Proposed Reopening of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 and Concurrent Stock Repurchase MONACO, May 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Scorpio Tankers Inc. (NYSE: STNG) (the “Company”) announced today its intention to offer $150.0 million aggregate principal amount of additional 1.75% convertible senior notes due 2031 (the “New Notes”) in a private offering (the “Offering”) to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), subject to market conditions and other factors. The New Notes will be issued pursuant to the same indenture as the Company’s $375.0 million aggregate principal amount of 1.75% convertible senior notes due 2031 (the “Initial Notes” and, together with the New Notes, the “Notes”) issued on April 10, 2026 and will form a part of the same series of Notes as the Initial Notes. Although the New Notes will initially trade under a different Rule 144A CUSIP number than the Initial Notes, the Company expects that once de-legended, the New Notes will trade with the same CUSIP number as the Initial Notes. The Company also expects to grant to the initial purchaser of the New Notes an option to purchase, during a 13-day period, beginning on, and including, the first date on which the New Notes are issued, up to an additional $22.5 million aggregate principal amount of New Notes. The Company expects to use a portion of the net proceeds from the Offering to repurchase shares of its common stock (the “Common Stock”), concurrently with the closing of the Offering. The Company expects to repurchase shares sold short by initial investors in the Offering in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through the initial purchaser or an affiliate at a price per share equal to the closing price of the Common Stock on the date of the pricing of the Offering. The Notes are senior, unsecured obligations of the Company. The Notes will mature on April 15, 2031, unless earlier converted or repurchased or redeemed by the Company. The Notes bear interest at a rate of 1.75% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on April 15 and October 15 of each year, beginning on October 15, 2026. The interest payment to be made with respect to the New Notes on October 15, 2026, will include interest deemed to have accrued from, and including, April 10, 2026. The offering price for the New Notes will include such accrued interest. Prior to January 15, 2031, the Notes will be convertible at the option of the holders only under certain circumstances and during certain periods. On or after January 15, 2031, holders may convert their Notes at any time at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately preceding the maturity date. Upon conversion, the Notes may be settled at the Company’s election, in cash, shares of the Company’s Common Stock, or a combination of cash and shares of Common Stock. The initial conversion rate for each $1,000 principal amount of Notes is 9.9615 shares of Common Stock, equivalent to a conversion price of approximately $100.39 per share. The conversion rate and conversion price will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events. The Notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations), for cash at the Company’s option at any time, and from time to time, on or after April 20, 2029 and on or before the 41st scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, if the last reported sale price per share of the Company’s Common Stock exceeds 130% of the conversion price for a specified period of time and certain other conditions are satisfied. In addition, the Company will have the right to redeem all, but not less than all, of the Notes if certain changes in tax law occur and certain other conditions are satisfied. Except as described herein, the Notes will not be redeemable at the Company’s option prior to the maturity date. The redemption price will be equal to the principal amount of the Notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date. If certain corporate events that constitute a “fundamental change” occur, then, subject to limited exceptions, noteholders may require the Company to repurchase their Notes for cash at a price equal to the principal amount of the Notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable repurchase date. The Company intends to use (i) a portion of the net proceeds from the Offering to repurchase shares of Common Stock as described above and (ii) the remainder of the net proceeds for general corporate purposes. The share repurchases, or the expectation of repurchases, could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of the Common Stock or the Notes prior to, concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the New Notes. The New Notes will only be offered to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act. The New Notes and any shares of Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the New Notes, have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act or the securities laws of any other jurisdiction, and unless so registered, may not be offered or sold in the United States except pursuant to an applicable exemption from such registration requirements. This announcement is neither an offer to sell nor a solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor will there be any offer, solicitation or sale in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale is unlawful. About Scorpio Tankers Inc. Scorpio Tankers Inc. is a provider of marine transportation of petroleum products worldwide. Scorpio Tankers Inc. currently owns 87 product tankers (32 LR2 tankers, 41 MR tankers and 14 Handymax tankers) with an average age of 10.2 years. The Company has reached agreements to sell six MR product tankers and three LR2 product tankers, which are expected to close in the second quarter of 2026. The Company has also reached agreements for four MR new buildings that are currently under construction with deliveries expected in 2026 and 2027, four LR2 new buildings with deliveries expected in 2027 and 2029 and two VLCC new buildings with deliveries expected in the second half of 2028. Additional information about the Company is available at the Company’s website www.scorpiotankers.com, which is not a part of this press release. title: How to Choose Reliable Packers and Movers in Mumbai Without Getting Scammed
summary: Looking for reliable packers and movers in Mumbai? Learn how to avoid moving scams, compare movers, verify licenses, and choose trusted relocation services for safe household shifting.
body_text: How to Choose Reliable Packers and Movers in Mumbai Without Getting Scammed Moving May 21, 2026 687 Add to Reading List Looking for reliable packers and movers in Mumbai? Learn how to avoid moving scams, compare movers, verify licenses, and choose trusted relocation services for safe household shifting. Moving to a new home or office can be exciting, but it can also become stressful if you hire the wrong moving company. In a fast-moving city like Mumbai, many people fall victim to fake movers, hidden charges, damaged goods, or delayed deliveries. That’s why choosing reliable packers and movers in Mumbai is one of the most important steps for a smooth relocation. Whether you are shifting your home, office, furniture, or vehicles, proper research can save you from unnecessary stress and financial loss. In this guide, you’ll learn how to identify trustworthy movers, avoid scams, and select the best relocation company for your needs. Research the Company Background Properly Before finalizing any moving company, spend time researching their background. A genuine moving company will have: A professional website Verified Google Business profile Customer reviews and ratings Active contact details Physical office address Reading customer reviews is one of the best ways to understand service quality. Focus on reviews that mention: Timely delivery Professional staff Safe handling of goods Transparent pricing If a company has too many negative reviews or fake-looking testimonials, it’s better to avoid them. Check Legal Credentials and Licenses Reliable packers and movers in Mumbai always provide proper documentation and legal verification. Before booking, ask for: GST registration Company registration details Insurance support Official quotation and invoice Transport permits A trusted company will never hesitate to share these details. Avoid movers who refuse documentation or operate only through phone calls and WhatsApp without a registered business presence. Compare Quotes Carefully One of the biggest mistakes people make is choosing the cheapest option immediately. Extremely low prices often indicate: Hidden charges later Poor-quality packing materials Inexperienced labor Scam operations Instead of focusing only on price, compare: Packing quality Transportation methods Insurance coverage Loading and unloading support Customer assistance Always request a written quotation after a proper pre-move survey. This helps avoid sudden price hikes on moving day. Understand Insurance and Safety Coverage Moving involves risks like: Damage during transit Theft Accidents Water damage Professional movers provide transit insurance to protect your belongings. Make sure you understand: What is covered Claim process Compensation terms Additional charges for insurance Insurance becomes even more important for long-distance and interstate relocation services. Read Customer Testimonials and Social Proof Customer testimonials help you identify whether a company genuinely delivers quality service. Reliable moving companies often have: Positive Google reviews Video testimonials Social media presence Repeat customers Referral-based clients Detailed reviews explaining real experiences are usually more trustworthy than short one-line ratings. Red Flags You Should Never Ignore Here are some major warning signs of fraudulent movers: No office address No written quotation Asking for huge advance payment Unprofessional communication No insurance support Sudden price increase after loading goods Fake branding or copied company names If you notice any of these signs, avoid the company immediately. Reliable movers always maintain transparency and professionalism. Choose Experience Over Cheap Pricing A professional relocation company may not always be the cheapest, but they provide: Safe packing Skilled manpower Timely transportation Better customer support Stress-free relocation Paying slightly more for trusted services is always better than facing damage, delays, or fraud during shifting. FAQs 1. How do I choose reliable packers and movers in Mumbai? You should check company reviews, licenses, GST details, insurance support, and customer testimonials before hiring any moving company. 2. What are common moving scams in Mumbai? Common scams include hidden charges, fake companies, damaged goods without compensation, and sudden price increases after loading. 3. Should I choose the cheapest moving company? No. Extremely cheap quotes often result in poor service quality, hidden charges, or moving frauds. 4. Is insurance necessary during relocation? Yes, transit insurance protects your belongings from accidental damage or loss during transportation. 5. Which is the best packers and movers company in Mumbai? Many customers prefer StowNest as one of India’s most trusted storage and moving companies offering professional packing, moving, and storage services in Mumbai. 6. Does StowNest provide storage and moving services in Mumbai? Yes, StowNest provides household shifting, self-storage, business storage, and relocation services across Mumbai and other major cities in India. Conclusion Finding trustworthy packers and movers in Mumbai requires careful research, proper verification, and smart decision-making. Instead of choosing movers only based on low pricing, focus on reliability, experience, transparency, and insurance coverage. A professional moving company ensures safe handling of your belongings and provides peace of mind throughout the relocation process. If you want a stress-free moving experience with trusted professionals, choosing experienced service providers like StowNest can help ensure secure packing, safe transportation, and dependable relocation support across Mumbai. title: Efluvio Telógeno: La Caída Difusa del Cabello por Estrés

body_text: Te lavaste el pelo y el desagüe se tapó. Te peinaste y quedaron hebras por toda la almohada. Cada vez que te tocas la cabeza, salen cabellos. No son parches — es una caída generalizada , de todo el cuero cabelludo, y el pánico es real. “¿Me estoy quedando calvo/a?” es lo primero que piensas. Si esto te está pasando, y especialmente si hubo un evento estresante, una enfermedad, un embarazo o un cambio importante en tu vida hace 2-3 meses, hay una alta probabilidad de que sea efluvio telógeno . Y la buena noticia —la mejor noticia— es que en la inmensa mayoría de los casos es temporal y el pelo vuelve a crecer completamente . En este artículo explicamos qué es el efluvio telógeno, por qué aparece, cuánto dura y qué puedes hacer al respecto. ¿Qué es el efluvio telógeno? El cabello tiene un ciclo de vida con tres fases: anágena (crecimiento activo, 2-7 años), catágena (transición, 2-3 semanas) y telógena (reposo, 3-4 meses). Al final de la fase telógena, el pelo se cae naturalmente y un nuevo cabello comienza a crecer. Normalmente, entre el 10-15% de los cabellos están en fase telógena en cualquier momento. Perdemos entre 50 y 100 pelos al día sin que sea un problema. Pero en el efluvio telógeno, un evento desencadenante hace que un porcentaje mucho mayor de cabellos entre prematuramente en fase telógena. El resultado: caída masiva y difusa 2-3 meses después del evento. Diferencia con otros tipos de caída Característica Efluvio telógeno Alopecia androgenética Alopecia areata Patrón Difuso, generalizado Patrón definido (entradas, coronilla) Parches redondos Inicio Súbito, 2-3 meses post-evento Gradual, años Súbito, impredecible Piel Normal Normal Normal Es permanente? No — casi siempre reversible Progresiva sin tratamiento Variable Causa Estrés, enfermedad, hormonas Genética + DHT Autoinmune Afecta a mujeres? ✅ Muy frecuente Sí, patrón difuso Sí Si no estás seguro de qué tipo de caída del cabello tienes, es fundamental que un dermatólogo lo evalúe. El tratamiento depende completamente del diagnóstico correcto. Causas del efluvio telógeno Cualquier evento que genere un estrés significativo en el cuerpo puede desencadenar un efluvio telógeno. Estas son las causas más comunes: Estrés emocional intenso El estrés psicológico es una de las causas más frecuentes. No es “imaginación” — el estrés crónico eleva los niveles de cortisol, que afecta directamente el ciclo capilar. Eventos como la pérdida de un ser querido, divorcio, problemas laborales graves o ansiedad generalizada pueden actuar como desencadenantes. Post-parto (efluvio postpartum) El ejemplo clásico de efluvio telógeno. Durante el embarazo, los niveles elevados de estrógeno prolongan la fase anágena, resultando en un cabello más denso. Después del parto, al caer los estrógenos, todos esos cabellos “extra” entran en fase telógena simultáneamente. La caída comienza 2-4 meses después del parto y puede ser alarmante en su volumen. Pero es completamente normal y se resuelve sola en 6-12 meses. Enfermedades y fiebre Infecciones con fiebre alta, cirugías mayores, enfermedades graves (incluyendo COVID-19 ) son desencadenantes bien documentados. La fiebre alta por sí sola puede provocar un efluvio telógeno. Durante la pandemia, los dermatólogos vieron un aumento significativo de consultas por caída difusa del cabello 2-3 meses después de cuadros de COVID. Deficiencias nutricionales La falta de hierro (ferritina baja), deficiencia de vitamina D , dietas muy restrictivas, pérdida de peso rápida o trastornos alimentarios pueden desencadenar efluvio telógeno. El folículo piloso es un tejido de rápida renovación y es especialmente sensible a deficiencias nutricionales. Cambios hormonales Además del post-parto, otros cambios hormonales pueden causar efluvio telógeno: Suspensión de anticonceptivos orales Menopausia Disfunción tiroidea (tanto hipotiroidismo como hipertiroidismo) Síndrome de ovario poliquístico Medicamentos Varios medicamentos pueden provocar efluvio telógeno como efecto secundario: Retinoides (isotretinoína para el acné) Anticoagulantes Algunos antihipertensivos (beta-bloqueadores) Antidepresivos Antitiroideos Si empezaste un medicamento nuevo y notas caída del cabello 2-3 meses después, consulta con tu médico. No suspendas ningún medicamento por tu cuenta. Si experimentas caída difusa, un dermatólogo puede solicitar exámenes de sangre para identificar la causa. En Examedi puedes agendar exámenes de laboratorio a domicilio y consultar con dermatología sin salir de casa. ¿Cómo se diagnostica el efluvio telógeno? El diagnóstico es principalmente clínico. Un dermatólogo evalúa: Patrón de caída — difuso, sin parches, no localizado Historial reciente — eventos estresantes, enfermedades, medicamentos en los últimos 3-6 meses Test de tracción — toma un grupo de ~50 cabellos y tira suavemente. En efluvio telógeno activo, salen más de 5-10 cabellos fácilmente Tricoscopia — examen del cuero cabelludo con dermatoscopio: muestra un aumento de cabellos en fase telógena y una disminución de la variación del diembro capilar Exámenes de laboratorio recomendados Para descartar causas subyacentes, tu dermatólogo puede solicitar: Examen ¿Qué busca? Hemograma completo Anemia, infección Ferritina Deficiencia de hierro (causa muy común en mujeres) TSH / T4 libre Disfunción tiroidea Vitamina D Deficiencia (muy frecuente en Chile) Zinc Deficiencia poco común pero posible Perfil hormonal (mujeres) SOP, desbalances hormonales En Examedi puedes solicitar estos exámenes a domicilio y recibir los resultados en días. ¿Cuánto dura el efluvio telógeno? La duración depende del tipo: Tipo Duración Características Agudo 3-6 meses Un solo evento desencadenante. Se resuelve solo al eliminar la causa Crónico >6 meses (hasta años) La causa persiste o es recurrente. Requiere identificar y tratar la causa subyacente Recurrente Episodios repetidos Múltiples desencadenantes sucesivos. Cada episodio dura 3-6 meses Línea de tiempo típica del efluvio agudo Momento Qué pasa Día 0 Evento desencadenante (estrés, enfermedad, etc.) Mes 2-3 Comienza la caída visible. Hasta el 30-50% de los cabellos pueden entrar en telógena Mes 3-6 Pico de la caída. Es el momento de mayor angustia Mes 4-6 La caída comienza a disminuir gradualmente Mes 6-12 El pelo nuevo crece. Primero es fino, luego se engrosa Mes 12-18 Recuperación completa en la mayoría de los casos ¿Es permanente esta caída? ¿Quedaré calvo/a? No. Esta es la respuesta más importante de todo el artículo. El efluvio telógeno no causa calvicie permanente . A diferencia de la alopecia androgenética , donde los folículos se miniaturizan progresivamente, en el efluvio telógeno los folículos están sanos. Simplemente “se tomaron un descanso” y van a volver a producir cabello. Lo que puedes notar El pelo puede verse más fino o con menos volumen durante varios meses Puede notar cabellos cortos nuevos en la línea del cabello (signo positivo de regrowth) El volumen total puede tardar 6-18 meses en volver a la normalidad completa En casos de efluvio crónico, la recuperación es más lenta pero el pronóstico sigue siendo bueno ¿Cuándo preocuparse? Busca evaluación médica si: La caída dura más de 6 meses sin mejorar (podría ser efluvio crónico o alopecia androgenética) Notas parches sin pelo (podría ser alopecia areata ) El cuero cabelludo se ve enrojecido, con descamación o inflamación Tienes otros síntomas como fatiga extrema, cambios de peso, irregularidades menstruales Tratamiento del efluvio telógeno Aquí viene la parte que puede sorprender: el tratamiento principal del efluvio telógeno es… no hacer nada . O más precisely, esperar y tratar la causa subyacente . Tratar la causa Causa Tratamiento Deficiencia de hierro Suplementación con hierro (meta: ferritina >40 ng/mL) Hipotiroidismo Levotiroxina (receta médica) Deficiencia vitamina D Suplementación (muy frecuente en Chile) Medicamentos Evaluar cambio con el médico tratante Estrés Psicoterapia, técnicas de manejo del estrés ¿Sirve el minoxidil para el efluvio telógeno? El minoxidil puede acelerar la recuperación al estimular la fase anágena de los folículos. No es estrictamente necesario — el pelo va a volver a crecer solo — pero puede ayudar a que el regrowth sea más rápido y visible. Algunos dermatólogos lo recomiendan cuando la caída es muy impactante emocionalmente o cuando el paciente necesita ver resultados. Lo que NO funciona Finasterida o dutasterida — estos fármacos bloquean la DHT, que no es la causa del efluvio telógeno. No tienen utilidad aquí. Vitaminas capilares sin deficiencia demostrada — si tus niveles de hierro, vitamina D y zinc están normales, tomar suplementos “para el pelo” no va a acelerar la recuperación. Champús anticaída — no hay evidencia de que funcionen para el efluvio telógeno. Evitar lavarte el pelo — el pelo que se cae en la ducha ya estaba destinado a caerse. No lavarte no evita la caída, solo acumula suciedad. Cómo manejar la angustia mientras esperas El efluvio telógeno es una de las condiciones dermatológicas más angustiantes precisamente porque la caída es tan visible. Algunas estrategias prácticas: Cuenta los pelos solo una vez — si pierdes >100/día, confirma el diagnóstico. Luego deja de contar. No ayuda. Usa productos voluminizadores — champús y acondicionadores que dan volumen visual mientras el pelo recupera densidad Cambia el peinado — cortes más cortos hacen que la caída sea menos notoria No te Collections el pelo con fuerza — accesorios tirantes pueden causar tracción adicional Sé paciente — el regrowth es lento pero seguro ¿Qué hacer si crees tener efluvio telógeno? Consulta un dermatólogo. Solo un especialista puede distinguir entre efluvio telógeno, alopecia androgenética y alopecia areata . El tratamiento es completamente distinto para cada una. Hazte exámenes de sangre. Ferritina, perfil tiroideo, vitamina D, hemograma. Identificar y corregir una deficiencia puede acelerar dramáticamente la recuperación. Identifica el desencadenante. ¿Tuvo algo hace 2-3 meses? Enfermedad, estrés, cambio de medicamento, embarazo. Ten paciencia. El pelo va a volver. El efluvio telógeno es temporal por naturaleza. No automediques con tratamientos para calvicie. La finasterida y la dutasterida son para alopecia androgenética, no para efluvio telógeno. En Examedi puedes agendar una teleconsulta con dermatología y solicitar exámenes de sangre a domicilio . Un especialista puede confirmar el diagnóstico y recomendarte el mejor camino. Preguntas frecuentes sobre el efluvio telógeno ¿La caída por estrés es permanente? No. La caída del cabello por estrés (efluvio telógeno) es temporal en la inmensa mayoría de los casos. Una vez que se resuelve el factor estresante o se trata la causa subyacente, el pelo vuelve a crecer completamente en 6-12 meses. ¿Cuántos pelos se caen al día con efluvio telógeno? Pueden caerse 200 a 500+ pelos por día durante el pico del efluvio, comparado con los 50-100 normales. Es una cantidad alarmante pero temporal. No significa que te quedarás calvo/a — los folículos están intactos. ¿Puede el efluvio telógeno convertirse en calvicie permanente? No directamente. El efluvio telógeno por sí solo no causa calvicie permanente. Sin embargo, si tienes predisposición genética a la alopecia androgenética , el efluvio puede “revelar” una caída que ya estaba en camino. Un dermatólogo puede distinguir ambos cuadros. ¿El COVID-19 puede causar efluvio telógeno? Sí. La infección por COVID-19 es un desencadenante bien documentado de efluvio telógeno. La caída comienza típicamente 2-3 meses después de la infección y se resuelve en 6-9 meses. No requiere tratamiento específico más allá de corregir deficiencias si las hay. ¿Debo tomar vitaminas para el pelo? Solo si tienes una deficiencia demostrada en exámenes de sangre. Tomar biotina, zinc u otras vitaminas “para el pelo” sin deficiencia no tiene evidencia de beneficio y puede incluso interferir con algunos exámenes de laboratorio. Primero mide, luego suplementa.
